clue.text: Money is smuggled into Liverpool perhaps

indicators.note: smuggled goods are slipped into something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Liverpool is an example of a football club, FC
to smuggle is to run (contraband), past tense RAN

explanation.surface: Cash being sneaked into a northern English port city.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool here is the football club, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and is still that of Switzerland, so it is a kind of money.

clue.text: Ill-dressed bum wearing mullet?

indicators.note: wearing means the fish has the bottom piece on it, enclosing it

parts.note: a mullet is a kind of fish; the question mark flags the hairstyle red herring
bum is slang for the rump, the buttocks

explanation.surface: A down-and-out sporting a mullet haircut looks badly dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mullet' wants to be the hairstyle; here it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpish means dowdy and unfashionably dressed, so it describes someone ill-dressed.

clue.text: Acting upset still about rent for legal adviser

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for acting, as in a job title

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the word for rent
upset in a down entry turns the word for still upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: still in the sense of 'even so' or 'yet'
rent as a past participle of rend means torn

explanation.surface: Performing a role while upset about the rent, someone seeks a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is torn, not money paid to a landlord; YET reversed by 'upset' gives TEY, which goes 'about' TORN.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a lawyer, especially in the US, who advises and acts for clients.

clue.text: Ravel tune? No, a composer of the same period

indicators.note: to ravel is to tangle, so the following letters are rearranged; Ravel is also a composer

explanation.surface: Asking whether a piece is a Ravel tune, and being told it is by another composer of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the French composer but is the instruction to tangle TUNE NO A COMPOSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemporaneous means existing or happening during the same time.

clue.text: Look for one turning to deception, mostly of old folk

indicators.note: turning round makes the two pieces before it read backwards

parts.note: look in the sense of appearance or manner, an air
for one means for example, e.g.

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for deception is used

parts.note: a deception is a trick

explanation.surface: Someone seeking a person who has turned to trickery, with the elderly involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses AIR + EG to give GERIA; 'mostly' drops the final K of TRICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatric is the adjective relating to elderly people and their care.

clue.text: One wet, marshy area? Contrariwise!

indicators.note: contrariwise means the other way round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
a bog is wet, marshy ground

explanation.surface: Asking about a soggy marsh, then being told it is quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrariwise' works twice: it reverses I + BOG, and the place itself is the opposite of a wet marsh, being a desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast dry desert in Mongolia and China, the contrary of a bog.

clue.text: Drum part, initially omitted, is being chosen again

parts.note: a drum for winding cable or thread is a reel

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for part is dropped

parts.note: a part of something is a section

explanation.surface: A drummer's part is cut at the start as a candidate is voted in again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drum' is a spool or cylinder, not the percussion instrument; 'initially omitted' drops S from SECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-election is the act of being voted back into office for another term.

clue.text: Anonymous fellow hounds my son at work for ages

indicators.note: set to work, the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An unnamed man pesters my son at his workplace, and keeps it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' looks like one phrase, but 'at' belongs to the letters being mixed and only 'work' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an extremely long time, as in 'never in a month of Sundays'.

clue.text: Supply aid — outstanding work

definitions.meaning: aid such as food and supplies sent to people in need
sculpture standing out from a flat background, literally out-standing

explanation.surface: Providing help, and doing it brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief means help for the needy, and also carving that projects from its background.

clue.text: Prosecute stalker? Essentially that's most appealing

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so the letters sit inside the words prosecute stalker

explanation.surface: Should a stalker be prosecuted? Basically, that would be the most attractive outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'proseCUTE STalker'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutest is the superlative of cute, meaning most charming or attractive.

clue.text: Locally one's beaten, left disfigured — that can't be justified

parts.note: in regional speech 'one' is said 'un, as in 'a good 'un'

indicators.note: disfigured means spoilt in shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone beaten up and left scarred — an indefensible attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disfigured' rearranges BEATEN plus L to make TENABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An untenable position is one impossible to defend or maintain in argument.

clue.text: Oscar's allowed to go around with a small hooter

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so the outer pieces wrap the inner one

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
allowed means let

explanation.surface: Oscar is permitted to drive about carrying a little horn.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hooter' is slang for something that hoots, here a bird, not a car horn or a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl, which hoots, is a small hooter in playful terms.

clue.text: Package tour's last chance for vacation in China

indicators.note: in places the two letter pieces inside the word for china

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word tour
vacating a word empties it of its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A package holiday's final opportunity for a trip to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate), giving PAL; 'vacation' empties CHANCE to CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a wrapped package sent by post, so the noun swaps directly.

clue.text: Lacking support, snooker player is so impatient

parts.note: the rest is the cue support used in snooker
lacking something means without it, -less

explanation.surface: A snooker player with no cue rest becomes fidgety and impatient.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the 'rest' is a stick used to support the cue on long shots, so a player lacking one is cryptically rest-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless means unable to keep still or settle, much like being impatient.

clue.text: Promoting Republican, agitate Royal noticeably

indicators.note: promoting moves a letter up, which in a down answer means earlier in the word

parts.note: to agitate a liquid is to stir it
kingly means royal

explanation.surface: A political campaigner backing a Republican stirs up the monarch conspicuously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promoting' lifts R one place up STIR to make STRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikingly means in a way that catches attention, which is to say noticeably.

clue.text: Where in Victoria perhaps, man's keeping ewe and tup finally?

indicators.note: finally places the word for man at the end, after the animals

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep and a tup is a ram, so together they are sheep
to man a post is to station oneself or staff it

explanation.surface: A man looking after ewes and a ram somewhere in rural Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is the Australian state, not the London station or the queen; Australian farms there are called stations.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep station is a large Australian sheep farm, as found in the state of Victoria.

clue.text: Primary area involving Rome's the church

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the Italian word goes inside the word for primary

parts.note: primary in the sense of fundamental, basic
in Italian, the language of Rome, 'the' is il

explanation.surface: A main district including Rome has the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rome's the' is the Italian definite article IL.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, often granted special status by the Pope.

clue.text: English NCO hides in tree, getting dirty

indicators.note: hiding in something means being inside it, so these letters go within the tree

parts.note: a birch is a tree
SM, sergeant major, is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: An English sergeant hides up a tree and gets grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' links the wordplay to the verb 'dirty'.
explanation.definitionFit: To besmirch is to soil or sully, especially a reputation, which is to dirty it.

clue.text: Riot dispersed with tear gas around the northern entrance to the Tower

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters enclose the short dialect piece
a dispersed riot is broken up and scattered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t'

explanation.surface: Police break up a riot with tear gas near the gate to the Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' rearranges RIOT and TEAR GAS into TRAIORSGATE, and T (northern 'the', t') goes 'around' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Traitors' Gate is the water entrance to the Tower of London through which prisoners were brought.

clue.text: In retreat, hermit possibly conceals identity of a poet

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the built word is read in reverse
conceals means the shellfish wraps around the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a hermit crab is one kind of crab
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A recluse on a retreat keeps secret who a poet really is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hermit' wants to be a recluse; it is a hermit crab.
explanation.definitionFit: Bardic is the adjective of bard, a poet, so it means relating to a poet.

clue.text: Fate of dimwit accompanied by some laughter

parts.note: clot is British slang for a dimwit
ho is part of 'ho ho', a laugh

explanation.surface: The destiny of a fool, met with a bit of laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fate' is one of the three Fates of Greek myth, not destiny in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho is the Fate who spins the thread of life in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Continent, oddly not one seen in map collection

indicators.note: seen in means these letters appear inside the word for a book of maps

parts.note: an atlas is a bound collection of maps

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of the word not

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A continent strangely missing from a book of maps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps N and T from NOT, which with I go inside ATLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary lost continent said to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Advise having institute for old and frail

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means substituting it, here swapping a letter

parts.note: to advise someone is to inform them

explanation.surface: Advice given at an institution for the elderly and weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' replaces the O of INFORM with I.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means physically weak, especially through age, which is what frail describes.

clue.text: Drop one in it!

indicators.note: in means the letter for one goes inside the word for it

parts.note: it is slang for sex, and bed stands for sexual relations, as in 'good in bed'
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction to land somebody in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop one in it' reads like the idiom for causing trouble; it is A put in BED.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead is a small drop of liquid, such as a bead of sweat.

clue.text: I show disapproval, but no university dons do likewise

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the word do is worn around these letters

parts.note: the word do is taken as itself

indicators.note: but no means the letter for university is removed

parts.note: tut is the sound made to show disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone tuts in disapproval, but the academics who aren't at university follow suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' is a verb meaning puts on, not university teachers; 'but no' removes the university letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, used to say one does or thinks likewise.

clue.text: Soldier wants a bit of work on retirement, loved one said

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: an erg is a small unit of work in physics

indicators.note: said means the word for loved one is heard, not written

parts.note: a loved one is a dear

explanation.surface: A soldier wants a bit of a job when he retires, his partner says.
explanation.walkthrough: AN ERG reversed by 'on retirement' gives GRENA; 'said' turns DEAR into the sound of DIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier of a grenadier regiment, originally one who threw grenades.

clue.text: Yes, decor's awful, not looking right?

indicators.note: awful decor is a mess, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that the room's decoration is dreadful and looks wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges YES DECORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a squint has eyes that do not point straight ahead, so they are not looking right.

clue.text: Do number one cut

definitions.meaning: British slang: to have a ... is to urinate, a number one
to cut with a sweeping blow

explanation.surface: Instructions to relieve oneself and then cut something.
explanation.definitionFit: Slash is British slang for urinating and also a verb for making a long cut.
